\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ملافه} (malâfe)}{ملافه (malâfe)}]{\fa{ملافه} (malâfe) — a bed sheet}

\label{lesson:FA-C439-malafe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a deposit, then the Persian for a safe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ملافه}}
\textbf{\fa{ملافه}} (\emph{malâfe}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bed sheet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{ملافه} \fa{های} \fa{تخت} \fa{تمیز} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Malâfe-hâ-ye takht tamiz bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sheets on the bed were clean.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{malâfe-hâ}. \emph{Malâfe 'avaz kardan} — to change the sheets.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{malâfe} was borrowed from Arabic: EtymDB derives it from Arabic \emph{milḥafa}, usually glossed 'a wrap, a covering cloth'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malâfe}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{malâfe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{malâfe}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a deposit, then the Persian for a safe, then say \emph{malâfe} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{روتختی} (rutakhti)}{روتختی (rutakhti)}]{\fa{روتختی} (rutakhti) — a bedspread, a bedcover}

\label{lesson:FA-C439-rutakhti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a safe, then the Persian for a bed sheet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{روتختی}}
\textbf{\fa{روتختی}} (\emph{rutakhti}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bedspread, a bedcover\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{روتختی} \fa{اتاق} \fa{ما} \fa{آبی} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Rutakhti-ye otâq-e mâ âbi bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bedspread in our room was blue.
\end{quote}

\emph{ru} 'on' + \emph{takht} 'bed' + \emph{-i}: what goes on the bed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{rutakhti} is a native compound of \emph{ru} 'face, on top of', \emph{takht} 'bed, throne' and the ending \emph{-i}. EtymDB does not list the compound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کولر} (kuler)}{کولر (kuler)}]{\fa{کولر} (kuler) — an air conditioner; an air cooler}

\label{lesson:FA-C439-kuler}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bed sheet, then the Persian for a bedspread.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کولر}}
\textbf{\fa{کولر}} (\emph{kuler}) — \textquotedblleft{}an air conditioner; an air cooler\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کولر} \fa{اتاق} \fa{کار} \fa{نمیکرد} \fa{و} \fa{هوا} \fa{گرم} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kuler-e otâq kâr nemikard va havâ garm bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The room's air conditioner wasn't working and it was hot.
\end{quote}

In Iran the \emph{kuler-e âbi} cools the air with water; the \emph{kuler-e gâzi} is a true air conditioner.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kuler} was borrowed from English and is usually traced to English \emph{cooler}. EtymDB does not list the Persian word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شوفاژ} (shufâzh)}{شوفاژ (shufâzh)}]{\fa{شوفاژ} (shufâzh) — central heating; a radiator}

\label{lesson:FA-C439-shufazh}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bedspread, then the Persian for an air conditioner.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شوفاژ}}
\textbf{\fa{شوفاژ}} (\emph{shufâzh}) — \textquotedblleft{}central heating; a radiator\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{زمستان} \fa{شوفاژ} \fa{اتاق} \fa{گرم} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar zemestân shufâzh-e otâq garm ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In winter the radiator in the room is warm.
\end{quote}

One word for the system and for each radiator.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shufâzh} was borrowed from French \emph{chauffage} 'heating' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{منظره} (manzare)}{منظره (manzare)}]{\fa{منظره} (manzare) — a view, a scene}

\label{lesson:FA-C439-manzare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for an air conditioner, then the Persian for central heating.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{منظره}}
\textbf{\fa{منظره}} (\emph{manzare}) — \textquotedblleft{}a view, a scene\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{از} \fa{پنجره} \fa{اتاق} \fa{منظره} \fa{دریا} \fa{را} \fa{میدیدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Az panjere-ye otâq manzare-ye daryâ râ mididim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
From the room's window we had a view of the sea.
\end{quote}

Arabic plural \emph{manâzer}. \emph{Manzare-ye zibâ} — a lovely view.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{manzare} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{manẓara} (EtymDB), a word built on the same root as \emph{nazar} 'look, view'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
